Each staging index has one block-stride writer; existing first CTA barrier publishes reach and cached indices.
Card loops are the only readers of cached indices. Every thread reaches the added barrier after its card/partial loops.
Only after that barrier does every thread write its original float total_parts slot. Original reduction barriers/order and final consumers stay exact.
Union arms both25632bitwords with matching alignment; no additional static or dynamic scratch allocation authored.
No union word is read as the other type; indices are dead before float stores, and every subsequently consumed float slot is initialized as before.
global_access_model: Total card_idx words read per CTA are unchanged for valid ordered spans: cached prefix once cooperatively, remaining words once through fallback. Coalescing and instruction locality are hypotheses, not measured transaction counts or speed. Two extra boundary loads and one additional barrier can outweigh them.
